images.clustering: None; one isolated large vessel in the NE part of q4.
images.notes: Clear, uniform water. q4 (~1110,115): one distinctly orange/red-hulled vessel, about 25 px long, with a wake trailing to the NE. That means it is heading roughly SW, which is neither NW nor SE, so it is left out of the heading counts. q2 right edge (~1495,330): a faint V-shaped wake, counted as one small moving vessel. Not counted: thin bright streaks at q1 (~1300,940) and q4 (~1370,500), possibly small boats. Quoin islets in q4 excluded.

Heavy sun glint, surface slicks and mottled texture across q1, q2 and q3 make small or dark hulls hard to see. q2: a long straight bright wake runs from the top-right corner (~1490,10) toward the SW (~1250,370). The hull sits at the tile corner, so this was counted as one medium vessel heading NE, with the size uncertain and no NW/SE heading assigned. q3: several thin V-shaped wakes near (~830,900), (~990,920) and (~700,1050); two were counted as small moving boats. The long curved line in q4 is a slick or current front, not a wake.

Clean, calm water with good visibility. No large or medium vessels anywhere. Not counted: tiny bright specks with no wake at q3 (~1230,410-435) and (~890,590), and q4 (~680,415). They could be small boats or noise.

Many small cumulus clouds and their shadows cover q2 and the NE edge of q1 and q4. That is far more than the 0.12% cloud mask reports; visible cloud plus shadow is roughly 8-10%. No vessels were seen in the clear water. Not counted: a faint short streak in q3 (~940,870).

summary.qualitative: Shipping in the lanes box was very sparse in all four images. The month showed one large vessel (June 1) and one probable medium vessel inferred from a wake (June 11); June 18 and June 21 showed no large or medium ships. Every vessel detected was under way, and there were no stationary groups, queues or anchorages.
